recipes.title: Add a new Symfony console code generation command
applies_when: The task is to scaffold or generate new GraphQL-related artifacts from SDL through CLI.
Existing Generate*Command patterns are the closest analog.
workflow: Mirror the Generate*Command class structure: constructor dependency injection, configure(), execute(), and SymfonyStyle output.
Register the command in FlexibleGraphqlExtension::registerCommands() with a console.command tag and constructor arguments derived from processed config.
If the command changes public usage, update README.md command guidance and any relevant quick install docs.
required_checks: Confirm command namespace stays under flexible_graphql:* if consistent with current patterns.
If a consumer app is available, run bin/console list flexible_graphql and the new command path.
Ensure docs stay aligned with any new public command.
common_pitfalls: Adding the command class without registering it in the extension.
Forgetting that execution usually happens in a consumer app, not the bundle repo.
Changing public command behavior without updating docs.
recipes.expected_result: A new flexible_graphql:* command is wired through Symfony DI and documented for consumer use.

recipes.title: Change or add flexible_graphql configuration
applies_when: The task touches defaults, enum values, consumer options, or config-driven runtime behavior.
workflow: Update Configuration.php first because it is the config tree source of truth.
Update FlexibleGraphqlExtension wiring if the new or changed option affects builders, commands, cache warm, or service aliases.
Synchronize src/Resources/config/flexible_graphql.yaml and README/docs examples so consumers see the same contract.
If the change affects runtime behavior, inspect change-impact and testing guidance before finishing.
required_checks: Compare defaults across Configuration.php, sample YAML, and docs to eliminate drift.
If a consumer app is available, run bin/console cache:clear or the narrowest affected command.
Confirm any enum branch is handled in both config and extension logic.
common_pitfalls: Changing only Configuration.php and leaving docs/sample YAML stale.
Missing federation or executor branches in FlexibleGraphqlExtension.
Ignoring current mismatches such as enable_preload and template_language_version defaults.
recipes.expected_result: Consumer-facing config contract and bundle wiring stay synchronized across code and docs.

recipes.title: Change bundle service wiring or builder selection
applies_when: The task touches aliases, resolver tags, command registration, builder classes, or cache warmer wiring.
workflow: Identify whether the change belongs in services.yaml, load(), or process().
If config-driven, confirm the option exists and is documented.
When touching process(), verify whether compiler-pass registration assumptions need to be addressed or documented.
Update docs if the public integration behavior changes.
required_checks: Review command and cache warmer registrations if constructor arguments or aliases change.
If consumer validation is possible, run cache:clear and the narrowest affected flexible_graphql:* command.
Check change-impact for docs and related command files that may need synchronized edits.
common_pitfalls: Editing process() logic without noticing reduced confidence around compiler-pass registration.
Changing aliases or services without checking the default_resolver config contract.
Forgetting to update command wiring after changing builder constructor signatures.
recipes.expected_result: Service registration and builder selection remain coherent across extension logic, services.yaml, and config.

recipes.title: Debug GraphQL generation runtime flow
applies_when: A task asks how generated files are produced or why cache:clear / command generation is failing.
workflow: Determine whether the failing path is cache warm or a direct flexible_graphql:* command.
Trace config values for schema_files, schema_type, dir, and executor into the selected runtime path.
For federation cases, inspect both extension builder selection and SchemaCacheWarmer federation extension logic.
Use docs/index.md only to understand host-app HTTP consumption, not bundle-internal execution.
required_checks: Confirm schema_files resolves to actual SDL files in the consumer app.
Confirm generated target dir is writable in the consumer app.
If command-specific, validate missing directive/type/field/scalar error branches.
If runtime depends on process(), flag reduced confidence until compiler-pass registration is verified.
common_pitfalls: Tracing consumer HTTP code instead of the bundle generation path.
Assuming failures are repo-local when the bundle actually runs in a host app.
recipes.expected_result: The active generation path, config inputs, and generated-file outputs are identified with minimal scanning.

recipes.title: Change the default resolver behavior
applies_when: The task mentions default_resolver, fallback field lookup, or property access semantics.
workflow: Update DefaultResolver implementation and keep constructor dependencies aligned with services.yaml.
If the public default_resolver service or config expectation changes, update Configuration.php and docs/sample config.
Review whether generated code or consumer expectations depend on the old fallback semantics.
required_checks: Confirm the flexible_graphql.default_resolver alias still points to the intended service.
If a consumer app is available, validate a field access case that exercises the fallback.
Update docs if the behavior is part of the consumer contract.
common_pitfalls: Changing resolver behavior without checking the service alias.
Forgetting docs updates if default_resolver semantics are user-visible.
Assuming repo-local tests exist for resolver behavior.
recipes.expected_result: Default field resolution remains coherent across implementation, service wiring, and consumer contract.

recipes.title: Change bundle integration entrypoints or documented consumer usage
applies_when: The task changes how the bundle integrates with Symfony boot, cache warm, command availability, or documented consumer setup/controller usage.
workflow: Identify whether the entrypoint is in-repo code (extension/cache warmer/commands) or documentation-only consumer usage.
Update in-repo wiring first, then synchronize consumer docs so they reflect the actual integration path.
If touching compiler-pass style logic, flag or verify registration assumptions because bundle class evidence is minimal.
required_checks: Reconcile docs with code entrypoints and command availability.
If a consumer app is available, run cache:clear or list flexible_graphql commands.
Update high-signal docs if the public integration contract changes.
common_pitfalls: Treating docs controller example as local runtime code.
Changing integration behavior without updating consumer docs.
Missing FlexibleGraphqlBundle registration implications for compiler-pass behavior.
recipes.expected_result: Bundle integration and consumer-facing documentation describe the same runtime path.
